target_customer: Engineering organisations with many microservices, such as Xero, Canva and TripAdvisor
problem: Engineering teams lost track of who owned services and whether they met quality standards, often tracking them in spreadsheets.
product_category: Internal developer portal and engineering operations platform

founders.name: Anish Dhar
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2021: a developer at Uber whose team tracked 200 to 300 services in spreadsheets.

founders.name: Ganesh Datta
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CTO on the company site; prior employers not sourced from an opened page.

founders.name: Nikhil Unni
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; TechCrunch names him a co-founder.

competitors.name: Backstage (Spotify)
competitors.what: Open source framework for building internal developer portals with a software catalog

technical_complexity.rationale: A service catalog with integrations and scorecards is mostly web engineering and API integration.

defensibility.rationale: Once teams catalog services and encode scorecards the data and workflows are sticky, but open source Backstage and rivals offer similar basics.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Backstage became a standard open source option and Cortex later marketed alternatives to it; Cortex deprecated its own Backstage plugin as of October 2025.

market_need_then: Microservice sprawl left teams tracking hundreds of services in spreadsheets, which TechCrunch cites as the founder's Uber experience.

branding.domain_note: Uses cortex.io; earlier getcortexapp handles on social platforms and docs on a cortextech.io domain per search results.

identity.voice_and_tone: Engineering leadership language such as Mission control for the AI software factory.

branding.brand_signature: DRIVE framework book for engineering effectiveness

rebrands.why: Product category expanded beyond the portal per the company's own product page.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear positioning content and a framework book, but no evidence of community, merch or press on the brand itself; the name is shared with Palo Alto's Cortex and others.

outcome_analysis: Cortex launched in 2019, shipped in March 2020 and has raised seed, Series A, Series B ($35M, 2023) and a $60M Series C reported at a $470M valuation. Sequoia backed it from seed. The company sells to large engineering organisations and has repositioned to an engineering operations platform. It remains independent and active in 2026.
notes: Seed is $2.5M per the press release and $2.25M per TechCrunch. The Series A $15M co-led by Tiger Global and Sequoia comes from an AOL syndication of TechCrunch; its month is not confirmed. Series C date conflicts: search results say 2024-09 while a Scale page was dated February 2026 by a search summary; valuation is Bloomberg-reported. A ServiceNow strategic investment exists but its amount and date were not found. One profile claiming Dhar and Datta worked at LendUp is single-source and unrecorded. The founders were in the Summer 2020 batch per the shard; Cortex page lists YC as Winter 2020 in some profiles. Competitor OpsLevel was not dated near the batch from sources opened.
